detail.title: Experimental Distinctions Between Autocatalytic Memory and Template-Directed Heredity
detail.summary: Autocatalytic networks can maintain history-dependent compositional states (memory) through non-equilibrium thermodynamic feedback, which is distinct from template-directed informational inheritance. While compositional persistence mimics memory through hysteresis, true heredity requires mechanisms that decouple information storage from simple thermodynamic relaxation, as proposed in frameworks modeling the emergence of natural selection.
detail.reason: Revising the notebook to integrate Prosser's thermodynamic emergence framework with existing evidence on autocatalytic networks, distinguishing compositional persistence from heredity.
